title: Ling Yuan Reappears
next_chapter_hook: The prophecy Ling Yuan left behind when he departed hung over Chen Ji's head like a sword waiting to fall. Before Chen Ji could catch his breath, undercurrents were already churning within the Sect—someone had already begun to act.

text.content:
The morning mist had yet to disperse, yet a thin layer of frost already clung to the spiritual plants on the Back Mountain of Tianqing Sect. Chen Ji stood beneath the eaves of the Servants' Quarters, gazing toward the faintly visible direction of the Sect Gate, his brow slightly furrowed. The lingering ache from the three Heavenly Fate Values burning away within him still pulsed faintly—that was the Tianji Record warning him, a violent upheaval was approaching.

He closed his eyes, and the blurry images from the Tianji Record Fragment still churned in his mind: in three days, the Sect would face a great calamity. But what exactly, the fragmented prophecy could never quite reveal. "Master Mo, couldn't you tell me what this 'upheaval' actually is?" he asked in his heart.

The guardian of the remnant soul fell silent for a moment before his aged voice drifted forth: "The Tianji Record only warns, it does not solve riddles. Boy, you should know—the more you know, the faster you die." The words were harsh, yet carried a hint of concern. A faint smile touched Chen Ji's lips: "Don't worry, I'm not done living yet." The moment his words faded, a chilling pressure suddenly emanated from the direction of the Sect Gate, like an ancient fierce beast awakening, slowly opening its eyes.

The pressure came without warning, yet pressed down on every disciple of Tianqing Sect like a tangible weight. Some gasped in shock, others felt their legs go weak, and some even collapsed to the ground, their faces pale as paper.

"This is... the scent of the Demonic Path!" an Inner Disciple cried out, his voice trembling.

Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply. His perception was far keener than ordinary people—the pressure carried within it a familiar scent that made him nauseous—traces of the "Heavenly Will" he had only glimpsed occasionally in the Tianji Record Fragment. He raised his head abruptly, looking toward the Sect Gate, where a black figure stood suspended in mid-air, surrounded by billowing black mist like an evil deity descending upon the mortal realm.

And that face, even from hundreds of zhang away, Chen Ji recognized at a glance—

It was Ling Yuan.

The "former Sect Master of Tianqing Sect" who should have died twenty years ago in the Demonic Path war.

dialogue.content: "Children of Tianqing Sect, do you still remember this old man?" The voice was not booming, yet it entered each person's ears with perfect clarity, carrying an eerie penetrating force that made scalps tingle. Ling Yuan's black mist slowly dispersed, revealing a face that was aged yet vibrant. His gaze swept across the terrified crowd below, finally landing on a certain direction—where Chen Ji stood.\n\n"Oh?" Ling Yuan let out a meaningful chuckle, "It seems someone recognizes this old man."

text.content:
Chen Ji felt a chill surge from the soles of his feet straight to the crown of his head. He had never met Ling Yuan, yet the fragmented prophecies from the Tianji Record Fragment had shown him this face countless times—that twisted visage hidden beneath a veneer of benevolence.

"Ling Yuan..." he murmured the name softly, his voice so calm it surprised even himself, "Seventh generation Sect Master of Tianqing Sect, who 'fell in battle' twenty years ago during the Demonic Path siege." He paused, a faint arc curving his lips, "Didn't expect you to still be alive, Elder."

At Chen Ji's words, Ling Yuan's smile widened further. He descended slowly, landing ten zhang before Chen Ji. The pressure around him did not diminish but instead intensified, forcing the surrounding disciples to retreat repeatedly, yet it alone spared Chen Ji.

"So you're that 'waste' Chen Ji?" Ling Yuan scrutinized him up and down, his gaze sharp as a blade, "This old man has indeed heard your name—the废物 of Tianqing Sect, a waste among servants." He shook his head as if in regret, "Such a pity, had you been born twenty years earlier, perhaps you might have caught this old man's eye."

dialogue.content:
Upon hearing this, Chen Ji did not fly into a rage. Instead, he displayed the most obedient smile imaginable—a smile so docile it resembled a lamb awaiting slaughter. "The Elder speaks truly." He bowed slightly, his demeanor so respectful it was impeccable, "The junior truly is a waste; surviving this long is blessing enough." He raised his head, a flash of cold light flickering in his eyes, "Does the Elder wish to reminisce about old times on this visit, or... give some guidance?"

Ling Yuan narrowed his eyes, his scrutinizing gaze lingering on Chen Ji's face for a long moment. He had met too many people who feigned ignorance, yet the "waste" persona of this young man before him made him feel an inexplicable unease—it was too natural, as if it were genuinely true.

"Reminisce?" Ling Yuan sneered, "This old man has no old times to reminisce about with Tianqing Sect." He stepped forward, the pressure suddenly intensifying, "This old man came today for one purpose alone—to retrieve what belongs to me."

choice.prompt: Ling Yuan's pressure bore down like a mountain, and all the surrounding disciples showed fear on their faces. As a "waste," how should you respond to this sudden nemesis?

choices.description: Continue playing the role of a废物, seeking opportunities to extract information. A figure like Ling Yuan would not lay hands on a Servant Disciple.
choices.visible_reward: Obtain key information about Ling Yuan's intentions
choices.risk_hint: May miss the opportunity to take the initiative

dialogue.content: "The thing the Elder wishes to retrieve, this junior, a mere Servant, wouldn't dare inquire about." Chen Ji bowed slightly, his posture lowered to the extreme, not even raising his eyelids, "The Elder may do as he pleases, the junior shall take his leave—" With that, he turned to depart, his steps light and unhurried, as obedient as a quail scared out of its wits.\n\n"Stop." Ling Yuan's voice rang out softly, yet like an invisible chain that froze Chen Ji in place. "Did this old man give you permission to leave?"

Chen Ji halted his steps and slowly turned around, his face still bearing that harmless smile: "Does the Elder have any other instructions?" Ling Yuan stared at him for a long while, then suddenly burst into laughter: "Interesting, truly interesting!" He laughed until tears nearly formed, "The废物 of Tianqing Sect lives up to its name—this ability to endure humiliation is a hundred times better than those Inner Disciples." The laughter stopped abruptly, Ling Yuan's gaze turned grim, "However, this old man advises you not to be too pleased with yourself—that thing on your person cannot protect you forever."

Chen Ji's heart tightened, but his expression remained unmoved. "The 'item' you mentioned, senior, this junior truly does not know—" Ling Yuan impatiently interrupted him, "Enough, stop pretending." He clasped his hands behind his back, speaking with arrogance, "I came here today not for a mere waste like you." His gaze passed over Chen Ji, gazing toward a certain direction deep within the sect, "What I seek is the current sect master of Tianqing Sect—that evil creature who usurped my position!"

Chen Ji's eyes flickered slightly as he calculated rapidly in his heart. Ling Yuan wanted to deal with the current sect master? This was unexpected... yet also情理之中. He lowered his eyes, concealing the gleam in his gaze. "Then... what does senior need this junior to do?" His voice remained humble, but carried more probing intent.

text.content:
Ling Yuan seemed highly satisfied with his obedient appearance. He took a pitch-black token from his sleeve and casually tossed it to Chen Ji. "Take this. Within three days, go to the entrance of the forbidden grounds at the sect's back mountain." His voice carried undeniable authority, "At that time, I will await you there. If you dare not come, or if you dare report this—" He lightly raised his hand, a black glow shooting from his fingertips, grazing Chen Ji's cheek and leaving a bottomless scorched hole in the stone pillar behind him, "Then you will know that even death is a luxury for waste."

With that, Ling Yuan laughed grandly toward the heavens. His form turned into black smoke and vanished from everyone's sight in the blink of an eye. The suffocating pressure also dissipated, but everyone present felt a chill down their spines—what they witnessed today would likely become a nightmare they'll carry for life.

Chen Ji stood in place, looking down at the cold black token in his hand. A cold light finally flashed in his eyes. Ling Yuan... As the Tianji Record showed, this old fool is still alive, and has deeply colluded with the Demonic Path. The three-day deadline, the sect's great calamity... So this is where it was destined to occur.

He laughed coldly in his heart: noted. When the timing is right, this debt will be repaid with interest.

choices.description: Appearing weak on the surface while secretly activating the Tianji Record to窥探 Ling Yuan's movements for three hours—even if it means sacrificing precious Heavenly Fate Value.
choices.visible_cost: Consume 5 points of Heavenly Fate Value
choices.visible_reward: Obtain key intelligence on Ling Yuan's actions within the next three hours
choices.risk_hint: Heavenly Fate Value is extremely precious; this may cause you to miss other opportunities

text.content:
In the instant Ling Yuan turned, a gleam of light flashed behind Chen Ji's lowered eyelids. His fingers subtly formed seals, and with a thought, the Tianji Record Fragment burst open in his Mental Sea—five points of Heavenly Fate Value ignited instantly, transforming into an esoteric force that pushed images of the next three hours directly into his sight.

The images flickered rapidly. Ling Yuan's figure appeared vaguely in the mist. He saw that after Ling Yuan left Tianqing Sect, he didn't go far but stayed at some secret valley in the back mountain. Someone was already waiting there—a woman in black robes, her face blurred, but her surrounding aura was incredibly strange, carrying a hint of familiarity.

"Heavenly Fate Lock Key..." Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply. That black-robed woman's aura perfectly matched the characteristics of the "Heavenly Fate Lock Key" recorded in the Tianji Record—something that could interfere with prophecies!

His sister... Chen Nian!

result_nodes.visible_reward: Obtain intelligence on Ling Yuan's actions for the next three hours, and accidentally discover clues about sister Chen Nian
result_nodes.risk_hint: Heavenly Fate Value consumed; plot direction becomes more complex

text.content:
After Ling Yuan departed, the sect erupted in uproar. The disciples who had just been terrorized by the pressure gathered in small groups, whispering to each other, their eyes filled with fear and confusion. "Ling Yuan... isn't he the former sect master who died twenty years ago?" "Demonic Path aura... How could he collude with the Demonic Path?" "We're finished, finished... Tianqing Sect is done for..."

Chen Ji paid no attention to these clamorous voices. He tightly gripped the black token in his hand, his knuckles white from the force. Three-day deadline, forbidden grounds entrance—Ling Yuan intended to use his hand to achieve some ulterior motive. And that black-robed woman in the valley...

His eyes grew darker. Chen Nian, his sister who had been missing for years. If that truly was her, it meant the Holy Sect had been making moves long ago, with Ling Yuan merely one of their chess pieces.

"Chen Ji." A cold, clear voice came from behind him. Chen Ji knew without turning who it was—Su Qingyao. She had somehow arrived behind him, her beautiful eyes shimmering with complex light, carrying both wariness and concern. "That person... do you know him?"

choice.prompt: Ling Yuan's sudden appearance has caused the situation to take a sharp turn. As a "waste" servant disciple, how will you deal with this unexpected turn of events?

choices.description: Since you've decided to trust Su Qingyao, truthfully tell her about Ling Yuan's token and the dangerous warning from the Tianji Record, seeking her support.
choices.visible_reward: Gain Su Qingyao's trust and possible assistance
choices.risk_hint: Relationship is still shallow; exposing too early may backfire

dialogue.content:
Chen Ji was silent for a moment, then turned around,直视 Su Qingyao's eyes. "Senior Sister Su." His voice was soft, yet carried an unprecedented solemnity, "In three days, the sect will face a great calamity." With that, he spread open his palm, revealing the pitch-black token, "This is what Ling Yuan left me—he wants me to go to the forbidden grounds entrance in three days."

Su Qingyao took the token, examined it carefully, her brow furrowed tightly. "Ling Yuan... that 'dead person' from twenty years ago." She raised her head, her gaze burning as she stared at Chen Ji, "How do you know all this?" Chen Ji met her gaze without dodging, "I... have some special abilities. I can see things I shouldn't be able to see." He didn't explain too clearly, but this statement was already a veiled admission of something.

Su Qingyao stared at him for a long time, long enough that Chen Ji thought she would press for details, but she merely sighed lightly. "Chen Ji." Her voice softened, "You trust me, and I trust you. Whatever happens in three days, I'll go with you."

Chen Ji felt warmth bloom in his heart, yet he still shook his head. 'Senior Sister Su, this matter is far too dangerous.' His voice dropped low. 'Ling Yuan's strength far exceeds our imagination, and—' He paused, his gaze flickering. 'In the Forbidden Grounds, there are probably even more terrifying things waiting for us. I cannot let you take this risk.'

Su Qingyao heard this, her brow slightly arching, a stubborn light flashing in her eyes. 'Chen Ji, did you forget who I am?' She stepped forward, closing in on Chen Ji, her voice cold yet carrying an undeniable authority. 'I am the Inner Sect Senior Fellow. My strength is more than ten times greater than your "trash." Do you have the right to make decisions for me?'

Chen Ji was stunned by her words. Looking into those determined eyes, he suddenly smiled—a smile carrying helplessness, relief, and a warmth he himself hadn't noticed. 'Fine.' he said softly. 'Then... together.'

Su Qingyao's expression softened slightly. She turned to gaze at the distant horizon, her voice drifting calmly: 'Chen Ji, whatever secrets you carry, there's one thing I want to tell you now—' She turned back, her gaze blazing like fire. 'In three days, no matter what happens, I, Su Qingyao, will never back down.'

text.content:
The two exchanged a glance, their understanding conveyed without words.

However, just then, an ill-timed cold laugh came from the nearby bushes: 'Tsk, quite the hero-saving-the-damsel scene. Too bad the male lead is trash, and the female lead is an arrogant大小姐.'

Chen Ji turned to look, only to see a young man in extravagant robes leaning against a tree trunk, watching them with an amused expression. Recognizing that face, Chen Ji's pupils slightly contracted—it was Han Lie, the number one genius of the Xuanwu Sect, Ling Yuan's loyal lackey.

'Han Lie?' Su Qingyao snorted coldly, stepping in front of Chen Ji, her eyes filled with vigilance. 'What are you doing at the Tianqing Sect?'

Han Lie jumped down from the tree, walking over slowly, each step carrying an insufferably domineering presence. 'Of course I've come to welcome our Ling Yuan Elder.' He grinned, revealing gleaming white teeth. 'And to see what本事 this Tianqing Sect trash actually has, to make Elder Ling Yuan come personally.' His gaze fell on Chen Ji, full of contempt and disdain. 'Kid, you'd better be smart. Hand over what Elder Ling Yuan wants. Otherwise—'

He didn't finish, but the naked threat was self-evident.

Su Qingyao blocked in front of Chen Ji, spiritual energy surging around her, clearly ready to fight. Yet Chen Ji gently tugged her sleeve, signaling her to stay calm. He stepped forward, that harmless smile still on his face. 'Senior Han, you're mistaken.' His voice was as gentle as a newborn infant. 'What Elder Ling Yuan? What thing? How would a lowly servant like me know about such things?' He blinked, looking completely clueless. 'If Senior doesn't believe, feel free to search me—though, if Senior makes a move, even though I'm trash, Senior Sister Su won't just stand by.'

This speech hid needles in cotton, both declaring his 'trash' stance and using Su Qingyao's presence to warn Han Lie. Han Lie's expression slightly changed, clearly not expecting this trash to be so troublesome. He exchanged a look with Su Qingyao, then冷哼一声, turning to leave. Before leaving, he glanced back at Chen Ji, a dangerous glint flashing in his eyes. 'Trash, remember this—I'll be waiting for you in the forbidden land in three days.'

choices.description: "Only reveal partial information, keeping the Tianji Record and sister Chen Nian's clues undisclosed, observe Su Qingyao's reaction before deciding whether to pursue deeper cooperation."
choices.visible_reward: "Keep cards close, maintain flexibility to advance or retreat"
choices.risk_hint: "Unequal trust may lead to betrayal at critical moments"

dialogue.content:
'Senior Sister Su, this is a long story.' Chen Ji weighed his words for a moment, choosing a middle-ground explanation. 'This person Ling Yuan... has some connection with me.' He didn't specify what connection, nor mention the Tianji Record, simply mentioning two key pieces of information: the 'three-day deadline' and the 'Forbidden Grounds entrance'.

Su Qingyao listened quietly, her brow slightly furrowing. 'That's all?' Her voice carried a barely perceptible disappointment. 'Are you sure there's nothing else you want to tell me?' Chen Ji lowered his eyes; that harmless face revealed no flaws. 'Nothing more.' His voice was soft, yet carried undeniable resolve. 'Some things, if spoken, would only bring trouble to Senior Sister.'

Su Qingyao stared at him for a long while before finally sighing. 'Fine.' Her tone cooled several degrees. 'Since you don't want to say, I won't force you. But Chen Ji—' She stepped closer, lowering her voice. 'In the forbidden land in three days, I'll follow you secretly. If you encounter any danger...' She paused, not finishing, but the unspoken meaning was clear enough.

Chen Ji raised his head, meeting her gaze. Those beautiful eyes held confusion, worry, and a hint of concern she might not have noticed herself. His heart stirred slightly, but he still nodded. 'Alright.'

text.content:
Night fell. Chen Ji sat alone in the Servants' Quarters, beneath the dim glow of an oil lamp, repeatedly examining the black token. The token was pitch-black like ink, its surface carved with a诡异 rune that faintly emanated an unsettling aura.

'This thing...' Master Mo's voice rang in his Mental Sea, carrying a weight of solemnity. 'Is the key to the 'Heavenly Fate Altar.''

'Heavenly Fate Altar?' Chen Ji's brow rose.

'That was a sacrificial site established by the Heavenly Dao's will during ancient times.' Master Mo's voice grew increasingly somber, as if recounting some forbidden knowledge. 'It opens once every century, using living people as sacrifices to absorb Heavenly Fate power... And Ling Yuan—he wants to restart the altar.'

dialogue.content:
A chill ran through Chen Ji's heart. "Using living people as sacrifices... So he wants me to go, for the sake of——"

"To make you the sacrifice." Mo Xiansheng interrupted without mincing words. "Or rather, to make the Tianji Record Fragment on your body the sacrifice. The Tianji Record itself is a Heavenly Fate object, sharing the same origin as the altar. If you can be offered up, the altar can absorb the power of the Tianji Record for Ling Yuan's use."

Chen Ji fell silent. He lowered his gaze to the token in his hand, his eyes cold and sharp. Ling Yuan... What a fine scheme of borrowing a blade to kill. On the surface he sent Chen Ji to his death, but in truth he was scheming for the Tianji Record on Chen Ji's body.

"However——" Mo Xiansheng's tone shifted. "This might also be an opportunity. Within the altar, the residual souls of past prophets are sealed. If you can survive the altar, perhaps you might obtain some unexpected fortuitous encounter."

A cold smirk curled at the corner of Chen Ji's lips. "Fortuitous encounter?" His voice was soft, yet carried a dangerous edge. "I'd rather see who grants whom a fortuitous encounter."

He tucked the token into his chest, closing his eyes. In his mind, the Tianji Record Fragment slowly unfurled—those blurry fragments of prophecy resurfacing once more: the Forbidden Grounds three days hence, Ling Yuan, Han Lie, and that black-robed woman who might be Chen Nian...

He silently calculated every variable, every move in this chess game. Ling Yuan had laid his schemes deep, but Chen Ji had never been one to wait passively for death. If you want me to go, then I'll go—but who lives and who dies is not something you get to decide.

---

Suddenly, a subtle sound came from outside the window. Chen Ji's eyes snapped open, his hand quietly slipping into his sleeve, gripping the Jade Pendant containing Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul.

"Don't be nervous." A hoarse voice came from outside the window. "It's me."

A figure tumbled through the window, movements as light as a cat. By the faint moonlight, Chen Ji recognized that face—it was Ye Qing, the Holy Sect's Saint.

"What brings you here?" Chen Ji's voice was calm, showing no surprise whatsoever.

Ye Qing straightened up and sat down across from him without ceremony, her heterochromatic eyes gleaming with an eerie light in the darkness. "I've come to warn you." Her voice carried a hint of gravity. "Ling Yuan, that old fiend, is far more dangerous than you imagine. He's not just colluding with the Demonic Path——" She paused, lowering her voice. "He is the Eye of Heavenly Dao's representative in the mortal realm."

Chen Ji's pupils contracted slightly. The Eye of Heavenly Dao... That ultimate villain had already been making moves?

"The Forbidden Grounds three days from now isn't merely Ling Yuan's trap." Ye Qing rose, walking toward the window. "It is the chess game laid out by the Eye of Heavenly Dao, and you... are merely the piece it wants to devour." She glanced back at Chen Ji, a complex emotion flickering in her eyes. "Chen Ji, you still have time to withdraw."

Chen Ji was silent for a moment, then suddenly smiled. "Withdraw?" He stood, walking to where Ye Qing was, meeting her gaze. "Ye Qing, you came specially to warn me—were you afraid I'd die in there, or afraid that your 'partner' would die and no one would help you escape the Holy Sect?"

Ye Qing froze for an instant, then laughed as well. "Both." She admitted openly. "But more than that... I just don't want to watch an interesting person walk to their death." She turned, climbing onto the windowsill. "Three days from now, I'll be going to the Forbidden Grounds too. Then, each of us gets what we need—as for who ultimately walks out alive... that depends on each person's own abilities."

With that, her figure vanished into the night.

Chen Ji stood by the window, gazing at where she had disappeared, his eyes glittering with intensity. Ye Qing... Holy Sect's Saint, yet controlled and used by the Holy Sect. Her appearance made the situation even more complex—but it also added more variables to this chess game.

"Interesting." He murmured to himself, the curve of his lips growing deeper. "Ling Yuan, Ye Qing, and the Eye of Heavenly Dao... It seems this show will be even more spectacular than I imagined."

He turned and returned to his bed, lying down, eyes closed. The three-day deadline was but a fleeting moment. And he had already made all his preparations—since you all want to play, I'll play along nicely.

Only, at the final moment, who is the chess piece and who is the chess player... that remains to be seen.

Outside the window, the moonlight fell like water upon the rooftops of the Tianqing Sect. And in some unobserved corner, a pair of eyes quietly watched it all—the will projection of the Eye of Heavenly Dao, observing every move Chen Ji made, a meaningful smile curling at the corner of its lips.

"Interesting..." That transcendent consciousness murmured. "This piece seems far more remarkable than anticipated. Perhaps... it's time to add some seasoning."

Before the words even faded, deep within a certain Forbidden Grounds thousands of miles away, a long-sealed seal quietly loosened by a fraction...

忽然，窗外传来一阵细微的声响。陈机猛然睁眼，手掌悄然探入袖中，握住了那枚藏有墨先生残魂的玉佩。"别紧张。"一个沙哑的声音从窗外传来，"是我。"一道身影从窗外翻入，动作轻盈如猫。借着微弱的月光，陈机看清了那张脸——是夜清，魔道圣女。"你怎么来了？"陈机的声音很平静，没有丝毫惊讶。夜清直起身，毫不客气地在他对面坐下，一双异色双瞳在黑暗中闪烁着妖异的光芒。"我来给你提个醒。"她的声音带着几分凝重，"凌渊那老东西，比你想象的更危险。他不只是和魔道勾结——"她顿了顿，压低声音，"他是天道之眼在人间的代言人。"陈机瞳孔微缩。天道之眼……那个最终大反派，居然早就在布局了？"三日后的禁地，不只是凌渊的陷阱。"夜清站起身，走向窗口，"那是天道之眼布下的棋局，而你……只是它想要吃掉的一枚棋子。"她回头看了陈机一眼，眼中闪过一丝复杂的情绪，"陈机，你还来得及退出。"陈机沉默了片刻，忽然笑了。"退出？"他站起身，走到夜清面前，与她对视，"夜清，你特意来提醒我，是怕我死在里面，还是怕……你的'合作者'死了，没人帮你脱离圣宗？"夜清一愣，随即也笑了。"都有。"她坦然承认，"但更多的……是我不想看着一个有趣的人去送死。"她转身，翻上窗台，"三日后的禁地，我会去。届时，你我各取所需——至于最后谁能活着出来……就看各自的本事了。"话音落下，她的身影已消失在夜色中。陈机站在窗前，望着她消失的方向，眸中精光闪烁。夜清……魔道圣女，圣宗的人，却被圣宗控制利用。她的出现，让局势变得更加复杂——但也让这场棋局，多了几分变数。"有趣。"他轻声自语，嘴角的弧度愈发深邃，"凌渊、夜清、还有天道之眼……看来这场戏，比我想象的还要精彩。"他转身回到床榻，躺下，闭上双眼。三日之期，转瞬即至。而他，已经做好了所有准备——既然你们想玩，那我就陪你们好好玩玩。只是，在最后那一刻，谁是棋子，谁是执棋之人……可就不一定了。窗外，月色如水，洒落在天青宗的屋脊之上。而在某个无人注意的角落，一双眼睛正静静地注视着这一切——那是天道之眼的意志投影，它看着陈机的一举一动，嘴角勾起一抹意味深长的笑容。"有意思……"那超越性的意识喃喃道，"这枚棋子，似乎比预想的更加出色。或许……是时候给他加点料了。"话音未落，远在千里之外的某个禁地深处，一道尘封已久的封印悄然松动了一丝……

text.content:
Over the next two days, on the surface the Tianqing Sect remained calm, but beneath the facade, undercurrents were already churning. The rumors of Ling Yuan's appearance spread like wildfire, unsettling everyone's hearts. Yet Chen Ji continued his daily servant duties, sweeping grounds, carrying water, looking every bit the obedient废物.

But only he knew how much he had done during these two days.

On the first night, he secretly contacted Ye Qing, obtaining detailed intelligence about the Forbidden Grounds from her—including the traps Ling Yuan might have set and the internal structure of the altar.

On the second day, under the guise of delivering tea, he quietly set up a contact signal outside Su Qingyao's residence. If anything befell him after three days, she would at least learn the news immediately.

As for the third day—

Before dawn, Chen Ji opened his eyes. He rose, dressed neatly, took one last look at this servant quarters where he had spent several years, then pushed open the door and stepped out.

Today was the appointed day for his meeting with Ling Yuan.

The entrance to the Forbidden Grounds at the sect's back mountain lay hidden within a gorge perpetually shrouded in mist. Normally, this was the Tianqing Sect's restricted area, off-limits to all disciples. But today, when Chen Ji arrived, he found someone already waiting at the entrance.

Not Ling Yuan—it was Han Lie.

"Waste of a thing, you're quite early." Han Lie leaned against the cliff wall, gazing at him with mockery, "I thought you'd run."

Chen Ji smiled without speaking. He surveyed his surroundings and noticed that besides Han Lie, several unfamiliar black-robed figures were scattered around, their auras strange—clearly experts from the Demonic Path. Ling Yuan had mobilized the Holy Sect's forces.

"Where is Senior Ling Yuan?" Chen Ji asked.

"What's the rush?" Han Lie jumped down from the cliff wall, walking up to him, looking down from above, "Senior said that before you enter, I should see what good treasures you're carrying." He extended his hand, reaching toward Chen Ji without any courtesy, "Hand them over obediently, and perhaps I'll let you die quickly."

Chen Ji stepped back, his face still wearing that harmless smile. "Senior Han, this is the entrance to the Forbidden Grounds." His voice was soft, yet carried a hint of imperceptible coldness, "If you make a move here and alert the sect elders, it won't do you any good."

Han Lie's expression darkened. "You're threatening me?" Murderous intent flickered in his eyes, "Waste of a thing, who do you think you are—"

"Enough." An aged voice came from the depths of the gorge, interrupting Han Lie. Then, a black figure slowly emerged from the mist—it was Ling Yuan.

His gaze fell upon Chen Ji, a playful smile curling at the corner of his mouth. "Little废物, you've come." He clasped his hands behind his back, his imposing aura restrained yet still giving an unfathomable feeling, "Good, quite punctual." He waved his hand, and the mist at the end of the gorge suddenly parted, revealing an ancient stone gate, "Go in. The answer this old man seeks lies within."

Behind the stone gate stretched a deep corridor, its walls carved with cryptic runes that emitted a ghostly blue glow. Chen Ji walked slowly inside, his footsteps echoing through the empty corridor, creating an especially eerie atmosphere.

"Be careful." Mo Xiansheng's voice rang out in his Mental Sea, "These runes are ancient formations—once triggered, the consequences would be unthinkable."

Chen Ji nodded slightly but did not stop his steps. He passed through the corridor and arrived at a massive underground palace. At its center stood a circular altar, covered in complex formation rune patterns that faintly emanated a Heaven-defying aura that made one's heart tremble.

Beside the altar stood two figures.

One was Ling Yuan, who had somehow arrived here before Chen Ji.

The other was a woman cloaked in black robes. She stood with her back to Chen Ji, poised gracefully, surrounded by a thin layer of mist that obscured her features.

"Welcome to the Heavenly Fate Altar." Ling Yuan's voice echoed through the palace, carrying a hint of triumph, "Chen Ji, do you know what this place is?"

Chen Ji stood at the edge of the altar, his gaze lingering on the black-robed woman for a moment, an ill foreboding stirring in his heart. "This junior does not know." His voice was very calm, "May this senior enlighten this junior."

Ling Yuan burst into laughter, the sound reverberating through the empty palace. "This is where all the prophets of generations met their end." He slowly walked toward Chen Ji, his eyes blazing with madness, "And also... the final resting place of your dear father."

dialogue.content:
Chen Ji's heart sank heavily. Father—the father he had never met, the man who had been chosen by the Tianji Record but ultimately 'died' at the hands of the Demonic Path.

"What... did you say?" His voice trembled slightly, a deliberate loss of composure. He needed Ling Yuan to say more, even if it meant playing the role of a son devastated by bad news.

Seeing this, Ling Yuan smiled even more complacently. "It seems you still don't know." He paced at the edge of the altar, hands clasped behind his back, his tone full of malice, "Your father, Chen Xuan, was once the inheritor of the Tianji Record, a hundred times, a thousand times more outstanding than you!" His voice suddenly turned harsh, "Unfortunately, he was too foolish—he actually wanted to resist the will of the Heavenly Eye—in the end, he died here, leaving no remains!"

Chen Ji clenched his fists, fingernails digging deep into his palms, but his expression remained a mixture of shock and grief. "You're lying!" he rasped, "My father was harmed by the Demonic Path—"

"Demonic Path?" Ling Yuan sneered, "The Demonic Path merely serves the Heavenly Eye. The one who truly killed Chen Xuan was none other than—this Heaven itself!" He spread his arms wide, as if embracing something, "And today, I shall use your blood, your Tianji Record, to restart this altar, to inherit your father's unfinished cause—to become the Heavenly Eye's spokesperson in the mortal world!"

Before his words even finished, the black-robed woman slowly turned around.

The moment that face entered Chen Ji's vision, his entire body froze—

It was a face bearing five or six similarities to Chen Ji, beautiful yet pale, with eyes holding no spark of life, like two pools of stagnant water. And on her forehead, a jet-black rune was faintly flickering—that was the mark of the Heavenly Fate Lock Key.

"Little Ji..." she spoke, her voice hoarse and hollow, "Brother..."

Chen Ji's pupils contracted violently.

That was his sister—Chen Nian.

The sister he had searched for all these years, standing before him now, yet no longer the memory of her. She had been completely controlled by the Heavenly Fate Lock Key's forbidden technique, becoming a puppet in the Heavenly Eye's hands.

"Satisfied?" Ling Yuan's voice sounded in his ear, carrying vicious delight, "This is the 'legacy' your father left behind—a good-for-nothing son, a controlled daughter. Tsk tsk, what an ironic fate!"

Chen Ji slowly raised his head, the deliberately maintained 'good-for-nothing' hue in his eyes fading away bit by bit, replaced by an abyss-like coldness.

"Ling Yuan." His voice was very light, yet it seemed to come from the depths of the Nine Abyssal Underworld, "You just said my father wanted to resist the will of the Heavenly Eye?"

Ling Yuan froze, seemingly not expecting him to ask this. "So what if he did?"

A cold smile slowly curled at the corner of Chen Ji's lips. "Then I shall... complete my father's unfinished cause on his behalf."

As the words fell, the Tianji Record Fragment erupted in his Mental Sea—with no hesitation this time!

Above the altar, the wind and clouds suddenly changed. A battle that had been destined from long ago, finally began...

Ling Yuan's expression flickered, though composure returned swiftly. "You?" he derided. "A good-for-nothing who hasn't even broken through Foundation Building, daring to speak so rashly?"

"Good-for-nothing?" Chen Ji repeated the word, then suddenly smiled—yet this expression differed sharply from his prior servile gentleness, cold and sharp, carrying a dangerous aura that chilled spines. "Ling Yuan elder, after all these years, haven't you learned something?"

He stepped forward, his bearing shifting abruptly. Though still appearing as a Menial Servant, he now radiated an impenetrable, oppressive presence.

"In this world—" His words came softly, yet each syllable reached every ear with perfect clarity. "A true good-for-nothing never refers to the weakest in strength."

"Instead, it's those fools who fancy themselves chess pieces, blind to the fact they occupy only a corner of someone else's board."

Ling Yuan's gaze contracted sharply. He finally grasped the deception—Chen Ji had performed this role throughout. An unsettling realization took root: decades of meticulous planning seemed to have been manipulated from the very start by unseen hands.

"You—" He barely began when a blade of sword-light erupted toward him—Chen Ji had somehow closed the distance, producing a short sword from nowhere, its edge cold as frost, aimed directly at his throat!

Ling Yuan moved with practiced speed, evading the strike while counterattacking with a palm strike that conjured churning black energy into a howling demon wolf, lunging at Chen Ji. Chen Ji twisted away narrowly, yet instantly pressed forward again, his short sword slicing three consecutive strikes, each one lethal.

Their exchange blazed like lightning, dazzling to witness. Ling Yuan's unease deepened—the "good-for-nothing's" strength appeared only at Qi Refining peak, yet somehow matched blows with an old monster at Core Formation stage. Those strange footwork patterns, precise foresight, perfectly timed dodges...

"Your Tianji Record..." Ling Yuan's realization struck him. "You've been using it the entire time!"

Chen Ji offered no response, his smile merely deepening.

Indeed, he had deployed it from the moment he entered the palace. Tianji Record's prophecies had flashed ceaselessly through his mind—Ling Yuan's attack trajectories, every weakness, every gap in his defense, all laid bare before his perception.

This was his true foundation.

This was why he dared storm this dragon's den alone!

"Ling Yuan." Chen Ji's voice cut through suddenly, ice-cold. "You think you're on the third level, but in truth, you're only at the first."

Before the words faded, his short sword erupted with blinding radiance—not ordinary Spiritual Energy, but an otherworldly pressure emanating from something belonging to "Heaven itself!"

The Tianji Record Fragment revealed its true power in combat for the first time!

Ling Yuan's complexion shifted completely...

text.content:
"In that flash of lightning, Chen Ji made his decision.

'Die!' He bellowed, his aura surging to its peak. The Tianji Record Fragment quivered violently in his Mental Sea, and a mighty Heavenly Dao force surged through his meridians into the short sword in his hand—the runes on the blade blazed to life, transforming into a brilliant golden sword light that shot directly toward Ling Yuan's vital point!

Ling Yuan's pupils contracted sharply. Too late to dodge, he could only forcibly mobilize all his spiritual energy, condensing a pitch-black shield before him.

BOOM—!

The sword light collided violently with the shield, erupting in a deafening roar. The formation rune patterns on the altar flickered wildly, and the entire palace trembled violently. Ling Yuan's shield cracked, shattered under the sword light's impact, and finally collapsed entirely!

'Impossible!' Ling Yuan let out an incredulous howl. 'A废物 at the Qi Refining stage, how could you—'

Before he could finish, the golden sword light had pierced his left shoulder, sending out a spray of blood. Ling Yuan stumbled backward, his arrogance replaced by terror. He stared at his blood-soaked wound, then at the '废物' before him with eyes cold as blades, finally realizing—he had lost.

Not lost in strength, but in calculation.

From the beginning, Chen Ji had known he would come to this altar; from the moment he stepped into the Forbidden Grounds, he had already fallen into Chen Ji's chess game.

'Chen Ji...' Ling Yuan gritted his teeth, his eyes full of不甘 and resentment. 'You wait. Today's humiliation, someday I will—'

'There is no someday.' Chen Ji cut him off, his voice cold without a trace of emotion. 'I told you, when the time is right, this debt will be settled with interest.' He raised his sword, its tip pointing directly at Ling Yuan's throat. 'Now, the time has come.'

Just as the sword was about to fall, a mournful shriek suddenly rang out—

'Don't!'

It was Chen Nian.

She had somehow broken free from Ling Yuan's binding and stumbled toward them, blood tears streaming from her eyes. Those once-empty eyes now flickered with struggle and pain.

'Brother... please... don't kill him...' Her voice was hoarse and desperate. 'He planted a forbidden technique in me... if he dies, I will too...'

Chen Ji's sword momentum halted abruptly. He gazed at this woman with a face full of blood tears and anguished struggle, his heart clenching like a blade.

This was the sister he had searched for all these years. Now she stood before him, yet controlled by a forbidden technique, becoming Ling Yuan's leverage against him.

Ling Yuan clutched his wound and laughed maniacally. 'Hahaha... Chen Ji, you dare not kill me!' He laughed wildly, savagely. 'If you kill her, you'll never forgive yourself for the rest of your life! Your father died this way—for saving her, he died by my hand!'

Chen Ji's hand trembled slightly, fury blazing in his eyes, yet he ultimately did not let that sword fall.

He turned to face Ling Yuan, the corners of his mouth suddenly curving into a smile more tragic than tears.

'Fine.' His voice was soft, yet carried a bone-chilling coldness. 'I won't kill her.'

'But you—' He raised his other hand, a ball of black light condensing in his palm. 'I will make you wish you were dead.'

The black light shot out and vanished into Ling Yuan's body. Ling Yuan's smile froze instantly. He惊恐地 discovered his spiritual energy was draining away at an uncanny speed—this was no ordinary seal, but a forbidden technique specifically targeting Tianji Record inheritors!

'You... when did you...' Ling Yuan's voice trembled.

'When?' Chen Ji softly repeated, his smile growing colder. 'From the moment you spoke my father's name.'

He had been waiting for this opportunity all along. Waiting for Ling Yuan to personally confess his grudge against his father, waiting for him to reveal a flaw, waiting for him to fall into the trap.

And now—Ling Yuan's spiritual energy was sealed, his meridians damaged, rendering him incapable of combat for a considerable time.

'Take him away.' Chen Ji said calmly.

As his voice fell, several figures flashed from the shadows—it was Ye Qing and her people. They had been lying in ambush, waiting only for Chen Ji's command.

'圣女...' Ling Yuan stared at Ye Qing, disbelief flooding his eyes. 'You betray the Holy Sect?'

Ye Qing coldly glanced at him. 'Betray?' She嗤笑一声. 'I was never a person of the Holy Sect—I was merely a piece they used.' She waved her hand, signaling her subordinates to take Ling Yuan away. 'Take him and interrogate him thoroughly. I want to know how much of the Heavenly Eyes' layout in the mortal world remains unknown to us.'

As Ling Yuan was dragged away, he continued to scream wildly: 'Chen Ji! Don't be triumphant! The Heavenly Eyes will not let you off! You think you've won? You're merely another puppet! Another—'

His voice gradually faded, eventually vanishing into the darkness at the end of the corridor.

On the altar, only Chen Ji and Chen Nian remained.

Chen Nian knelt on the ground, trembling all over, blood tears sliding down her cheeks. 'Brother...' Her voice was hoarse and desperate. 'I'm sorry... I'm sorry... I killed Father... It's me...'

Chen Ji walked slowly to her side and crouched down. He raised his hand and gently wiped away the blood tears from her face, his movements tender—a stark contrast to the man who had just been wielding his sword.

'Don't blame yourself.' His voice was soft, yet carried a reassuring warmth. 'You were merely being used.'

'But... Father...'

'Father's choice was to protect you.' Chen Ji cut her off, a complex light flickering in his eyes. 'If his spirit watches from heaven, he would never want to see you torment yourself like this.'

He stood and helped Chen Nian up. 'Come, let's leave this place.' His voice returned to calm. 'Ling Yuan is captured, the source of the forbidden technique has been severed. I will find a way to break the technique on you.'

Chen Nian looked up at this brother, both familiar and strange, and fresh tears spilled forth. 'Brother... you've changed.'

'Yes.' Chen Ji let out a soft laugh, his smile carrying a hint of bitterness. 'If I hadn't changed, I would have died.' He patted her shoulder. 'Come, we still have much to do.'

The siblings walked away together, disappearing into the depths of the altar.

Behind them, that ancient Altar of Heavenly Fate suddenly collapsed with a thunderous crash, raising clouds of dust. Secrets buried for twenty years, along with this earth-shaking upheaval, finally saw the light of day.

The landscape of the Tianqing Sect, the power dynamics of the three great sects, even the layout of the Heavenly Eyes—all would be fundamentally rewritten after this day.

Ling Yuan's prophecy still echoed in the air: the next meeting would be Chen Ji's death...

But now, the prophecy seemed shattered.

Yet the shadow of the Heavenly Eyes still hung over Chen Ji. Those transcendent eyes, from some unseen corner, quietly watched every move in his chess game..."

text.content:
Chen Ji sheathed his sword, his gaze falling on Ling Yuan. His voice was cold as frost. "Do you think I would sacrifice her life just to kill you?" A mocking curve twisted at the corner of his lips. "Ling Yuan, you overestimate yourself far too much."

He turned and strode quickly toward Chen Nian, kneeling on one knee before her. Cupping her face in both hands, he examined carefully the诡异的符文 on her forehead. "Little Nian, don't be afraid." His voice was extremely gentle, carrying a tenderness never seen before. "Your brother is here to rescue you."

Chen Nian stared at him blankly, blood tears still flowing from her eyes, yet her lips trembled slightly. "Brother... how could you..."

"Don't speak yet." Chen Ji interrupted her. "Let me examine the structure of this forbidden technique." He closed his eyes as the Tianji Record Fragment slowly unfurled within his Mental Sea, information about the forbidden technique flooding into his mind like a tide.

After a moment, he opened his eyes, a flash of determination crossing his gaze. "The core of this forbidden technique lies within the Heavenly Fate Altar." He stood up, shielding Chen Nian behind him. "As long as the altar is destroyed, the forbidden technique will naturally dissolve—but in that case, the remnant soul my father left in the altar will also dissipate."

Upon hearing this, Ling Yuan's face turned pale with shock. "You're insane!" he hissed. "That is Chen Xuan's remnant soul! If destroyed, you will forever lose the chance to learn the truth behind his death!"

Chen Ji turned his head to look at Ling Yuan, the smile at the corner of his mouth growing colder. "The truth?" he said softly. "I already know exactly how my father died." He pointed to his own eyes. "The Tianji Record told me everything—he chose to sacrifice himself to save my sister."

"And you—" His voice suddenly turned sharp. "Are nothing but the executioner."

As his words fell, he turned and struck the altar behind him with a palm!

"No!" Ling Yuan let out a desperate shriek, wanting to intervene but already pinned down by Ye Qing's men.

BOOM—!

The altar collapsed beneath Chen Ji's palm, countless particles of light rising from the ruins like stars scattered across the sky. It was Chen Xuan's remnant soul, and in its final moment of dissipation, it seemed to gently nod toward Chen Ji.

At the same time, the talisman on Chen Nian's forehead shattered abruptly, dissolving into wisps of dark mist that scattered. Her eyes regained clarity, and the blood tears gradually stopped.

"Brother..." she leaned weakly against Chen Ji, tears flowing again—but these were tears of joy after surviving a catastrophe. "I'm... I'm free..."

Chen Ji gently patted her back, yet his gaze remained fixed on Ling Yuan. "Take him away." His voice was calm. ""Take good care' of him. Don't let him die."

Ye Qing nodded and waved for his men to escort Ling Yuan away. Before leaving, Ling Yuan was still raving frantically: "Chen Ji! You will regret this! The Eyes of Heavenly Secrets will not let you off!"

Chen Ji paid him no attention, simply holding his sister quietly while watching those fading particles of light.

"Father..." he whispered in his heart. "Your son has avenged you." He paused, a complex light flickering in his eyes. "The road ahead, I will walk it... for you, and for myself."

The particles of light dissipated completely, leaving only broken walls and scattered stones among the altar's ruins.

And on this ground of ruins, a new chess game was quietly taking shape...

As Ling Yuan was dragged away, those resentful and venomous eyes stared fixedly at Chen Ji, as if trying to carve his appearance into his bones. "Chen Ji..." His voice squeezed out from his throat, hoarse and sinister, "Do you think this is over? The Eye of Heavenly Dao... will not let you go... When we meet again... that will be your death..."

This was the prophecy Ling Yuan left upon his departure.

Chen Ji stood atop the altar's ruins, watching that disheveled figure vanish into the darkness, his gaze utterly unruffled. He knew Ling Yuan's type too well—the closer to the abyss, the more desperate the counterattack. But what of it?

"Next time we meet?" he murmured to himself, a meaningful curve forming at the corner of his lips, "That depends on whether you'll have a next time."

The tremors from the altar's collapse gradually subsided, and secrets sealed for twenty years began to surface. The truth of the Heavenly Fate Altar, his father Chen Xuan's past, the Eye of Heavenly Dao's schemes... all of this would gradually be brought to light with Ling Yuan's capture.

Chen Ji turned to look at Chen Nian standing beside him. She had awakened, staring at him in a daze, her eyes filled with the bewilderment and disbelief of someone who had escaped death. "Brother... how... how did you become so strong?"

"If I wasn't strong, I'd be dead." Chen Ji's voice was calm, yet carried a heart-wrenching layer of vicissitude. "All these years, I've been searching for a way to save you." He paused, reaching out to gently ruffle her hair, the tenderness in his gesture a stark contrast to the man he had been moments before. "Now, I finally have a clue."

Tears welled up again in Chen Nian's eyes as she threw herself into his arms, sobbing incoherently. "I'm sorry... brother... I'm sorry... I was the one who害了 father... It's all my fault..."

Chen Ji gently patted her back, saying nothing. He knew that years of guilt and self-blame could not be absolved in a single day. But no matter—he had plenty of time.

In the distance, Ye Qing stood quietly in the shadows, watching this reunion of siblings, a complex light flickering in her eyes. She suddenly felt a pang of envy for Chen Nian—at least she still had a brother who would risk everything to save her.

"Chen Ji." She spoke, her voice returning to its usual cold detachment. "I'll handle the matter of Ling Yuan. But there's something I must warn you—" Her gaze grew solemn. "Ling Yuan is merely one of the Eye of Heavenly Dao's chess pieces. His capture doesn't mean the crisis is over."

Chen Ji nodded. "I know." He released Chen Nian and turned to face Ye Qing. "The Eye of Heavenly Dao's schemes run far deeper than I imagined. Ling Yuan, Han Lie, even the three great sects... they're all merely pieces on a chessboard."

"Then what do you plan to do?" Ye Qing asked.

Chen Ji fell silent for a moment, then slowly curved his lips into a smile—a smile calm, sharp, and carrying an unsettling calculation that could make one's spine crawl.

"What to do?" he said softly. "Naturally... continue playing the game."

"Ling Yuan thinks he's on the third level, while I thought I was on the second—actually, I've been in the stratosphere all along."

With those words, he turned and walked toward the palace exit, leading Chen Nian with him.

Behind him, Ye Qing watched his departing back and suddenly smiled. "Interesting..." she murmured. "Chen Ji, you're more dangerous than I imagined."

What she did not say was that perhaps allying with such a person was her best choice to escape the Holy Sect.

As night deepened, within a certain forbidden area of the Tianqing Sect, a storm that would reshape the landscape was quietly brewing. Ling Yuan's prophecy still echoed in her ears: the next meeting would be a death sentence.

But Chen Ji had never believed in prophecies.

He only believed in the will of the Chess Player.

And now, a new game had begun. Ling Yuan's capture, the Tianji Record's power first revealed, Chen Nian rescued... all of this was merely the prologue before the great curtain rose.

The Eye of Heavenly Dao watched everything from the shadows. That transcendent consciousness waited for Chen Ji to walk into its next trap.

After all, in the eyes of Heaven—

All pieces were ultimately just pieces.

Even the most outstanding one...

Dawn broke, and the first rays of morning light fell upon the rooftops of the Tianqing Sect.

Chen Ji stood at the cliff's edge of the sect's back mountain, gazing down at the mist-shrouded expanse of the sect below. Behind him, Chen Nian stood quietly, while Su Qingyao and Ye Qing flanked either side—these three were his most crucial assets.

"Next..." he spoke softly, his voice calm yet carrying an undeniable certainty that inspired confidence, "It's time to let the entire world know that the Tianqing Sect has a wastrel named Chen Ji."

With those words, he turned and strode toward the sect.

Behind him, three figures followed closely.

And in a hidden corner outside the sect, a pair of eyes belonging to the Eye of Heavenly Dao watched silently—this transcendent consciousness curved a meaningful smile in the darkness.

"Interesting..."

"This piece might be more valuable than I anticipated."

"It's time... to add some fuel to the fire."
